name: Claude Developer Platform
summary: Anthropic's agent stack on platform.claude.com: the Messages API and tool use, plus Managed Agents — versioned agent configs, per-session containers Anthropic provisions, an SSE event stream, MCP servers with vault-held credentials, skills, memory stores, and cron-scheduled deployments. Workspaces and the Admin API scope keys and resources; the control plane is Anthropic-operated, though tool execution can move to a self-hosted sandbox.

agent-runtime.note: Managed Agents runs the loop on Anthropic's orchestration layer: a persisted, versioned agent config plus stateful sessions with an event stream, automatic context compaction, and prompt caching.

orchestration.note: A coordinator agent delegates to a roster of subagents in parallel threads, and scheduled deployments fire sessions on a cron cadence — but there is no declarative multi-step pipeline or DAG the platform executes.

knowledge-memory.note: Memory stores persist versioned text documents across sessions, mounted into the container as a filesystem the agent reads and writes. There is no document ingestion pipeline, embeddings endpoint, or semantic search — retrieval is file reads, grep, and the hosted web search tool.

tools-integration.note: Client-side tool use with strict schemas, Anthropic-hosted server tools (web search, web fetch, code execution), remote MCP servers declared on the agent, and HMAC-signed webhooks for session state changes.

identity-governance.note: The Admin API manages org members, five org roles, workspace membership, and API keys; per-tool permission policies gate execution and session budgets cap spend. Authorization is workspace-scoped rather than a per-resource policy language, and there is no configurable guardrail model — content safeguards are built into the models.

observability.note: Every session exposes a replayable event history with model-request spans and per-request token usage, a live Console trace view, plus the Usage and Cost API and the Compliance API activity feed. Webhook delivery is best-effort — three attempts, then dropped, with no dead-letter queue to inspect.

data-secrets.note: The Files API stores inputs and captures session outputs, and vaults hold credentials the sandbox never sees: MCP OAuth tokens refreshed automatically, and environment-variable secrets substituted into outbound requests at egress with a per-credential host allowlist.

evaluation.note: An outcome states what done looks like and a separate grader scores each iteration against a rubric, looping until it passes or hits max_iterations. That is per-session grading, not a dataset and scorer API, and nothing gates a version promotion on it.

channels.note: No gateway for developer-built agents to Slack, WhatsApp, Telegram, or Discord, and no embeddable chat UI; integrations reach the agent through the API or MCP. Anthropic ships first-party Slack surfaces for its own Claude apps, which is a different thing from a channel gateway an agent you define can be bound to.

code-execution.note: Every session gets an isolated container where bash, file operations, and code run, and the Messages API exposes code execution as a hosted server tool. A self-hosted sandbox moves that execution to infrastructure you control via an outbound-polling worker.

human-in-loop.note: A tool carrying the always_ask permission policy pauses the session at the call, which idles awaiting a tool-confirmation event; the reply allows or denies, and a denial message is surfaced back to the agent so it can change approach.

multi-tenancy.note: Workspaces scope API keys, rate limits, spend, and agent resources — agents, sessions, vaults, and memory stores all belong to one workspace — with membership and roles assignable per workspace through the Admin API.

declarative-deployment.note: Agents and environments are checked in as YAML and applied from CI with the ant CLI, using a version field for optimistic concurrency. Each resource is applied on its own — there is no dependency-graph plan and apply over a stack, and no teardown that unwinds what a failed apply created.

agent-versioning.note: Every agent update creates an immutable, append-only version, and a session pins one by number — so rollback is pinning new sessions back to a known-good version while running sessions keep theirs. There are no aliases, no traffic split for a canary, and no gated promotion.

skill-learning.note: Skills are versioned resources an agent can read, and a read-write memory store lets it record learnings that later sessions mount — but promoting experience into a published skill version is a step you drive through the Skills API, not a loop the platform runs.
